newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields down after uninspiring day.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields down after uninspiring day.

text.p: *Australian bond yields closed lower after drab trading session with the market continuing to rely heavily on the U.S. for direction in the absence of any major local data.
*U.S. jobless claims, Philadelphia Fed survey due later.
Australian bond yields closed lower after drab trading session with the market continuing to rely heavily on the U.S. for direction in the absence of any major local data
Local bond futures were squeezed higher initially after U.S. Treasuries rebounded on Wednesday, but from then on the market did very little, traders said.

"I suspect you will see buying on dips at the short end in the run-up to the FOMC and the RBA board meetings. But at the moment they seem a long way away, particularly if we get any more days like today," one trader added.
The market is fully prepared for a further easing in monetary policy after the RBA board meeting on July 1 and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 and 2.

Traders said the pull-back in bond prices seen in the previous two sessions was long overdue, but the market now appears to have found a base and is priming itself up to retest the 3-1/4 year highs seen on Monday.
However, such a move will likely be dependent on the U.S. market, which faces the latest weekly jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey among a clutch of data later on Thursday.

The local market reversed its initial widening bias to the U.S. and extended its outperformance against Canada. Canadian debt fell sharply on Wednesday on the back of a sharp drop in the Canadian dollar.
